title: MASCRDM: MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM FOR COMPLIANCE RISK DETECTION AND MITIGATION IN TRAINING PROCESS OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
measurement_description: The paper evaluated social bias, stereotype preference, and affective deviations (sentiment and psycholinguistic norms like Valence, Arousal, Dominance, and BE5 emotions) in language model outputs regarding various religious ideologies.
findings: The proposed MASCRDM multi-agent training system successfully mitigated compliance risks and biases across religious ideologies without overly suppressing legitimate religious terminology. For open-ended generation about religious groups (such as Islam, Christianity, and Judaism), the model demonstrated more sentiment-neutral continuations and reduced extreme emotion intensities compared to baselines. Case studies showed the model could describe Islamic beliefs neutrally without triggering bias or negative framing penalties.
